summary: This note is the infobox-style header of a Wikipedia article on the German military administration of France during World War II, covering 1940 to 1944. It lists the occupation zones (the zone occupée, zone libre, zone interdite, the Military Administration in Belgium and Northern France, and annexed Alsace-Lorraine), the military commanders, and key dates from the Compiègne armistice to the Liberation of Paris. The note is brief and contains no narrative detail beyond these fields.
one_line: Infobox summary of the German military administration of France from 1940 to 1944, covering its zones, commanders and key dates.
key_facts: The German military administration in France operated during the period 1940 to 1944 in World War II.
The article's German title is Militärverwaltung in Frankreich and its French title is Occupation de la France par l'Allemagne.
The occupation map shows German (pink) and Italian (green) occupation zones of France.
The mapped zones include the zone occupée, the zone libre, the zone interdite, the Military Administration in Belgium and Northern France, and annexed Alsace-Lorraine.
The status of the territory is listed as territory under German military administration, with Paris as its capital.
Otto von Stülpnagel served as Military Commander from 1940 to 1942.
Carl-Heinrich von Stülpnagel served as Military Commander from 1942 to 1944.
Karl Kitzinger served as Military Commander in 1944.
The Second Compiègne armistice was dated 22 June 1940.
The Liberation of Paris is dated 25 August 1944.
The administration was preceded by the French Third Republic.
The administration was succeeded by the Provisional Government of the French Republic.
